title: The muscle tip's 'Why' sheet sends members to a Settings row that is not there
what: The 'Why we suggest this' sheet on a muscle tip ends with 'You can turn these suggestions off in Settings, Muscle tips'. Settings has no Muscle tips row. It sits one level deeper: Settings, Workouts, More workout choices, Muscle tips. A member who follows the words looks down the Settings list and does not find it.
expected: The line names the real way in (Settings, More workout choices, Muscle tips), or the sheet has a button that opens the Muscle tips page.
how_often: every time the Why sheet is opened
fix_line: Name the full path in the line, or add a button that opens the Muscle tips page

title: Two badge 'how to earn' lines describe a rule the app does not use
what: The big-day badges say 'Every set's weight x reps is added up'. The app's one rule leaves warm-up sets out, counts both dumbbells, and adds body weight on pull-ups and dips, so a member who adds up their own sets gets a different number. The early-bird badge says 'Start 5 workouts before 7 in the morning', but only starts from 4 am to 7 am count; a workout started at 2 or 3 am does not.
expected: The how-to lines say what really counts: 'kg lifted, the same number as on your workout summary (warm-ups do not count)' and 'between 4 and 7 in the morning'.
who: members who look at locked badges
how_often: every time the badge shelf is opened
fix_line: Reword the two how-to lines to match the rule

title: Two home programs need more gear, or a different number of days, than their description says
what: Home Upper / Lower says 'Body weight and a pull-up bar', but its routines also have bench dips (needs a bench or chair) and inverted rows (needs a low bar or table). Calisthenics says 'The three days rotate' while its line above reads '4 days a week', so a member does not know if it is a 3-day or a 4-day program.
expected: Each program's description lists all the gear its exercises need, and the day count in the description matches the 'N days a week' line.
how_often: every time those two programs are viewed
fix_line: Add the chair and low bar to the description, and say four days with three workouts in turn

title: The Strength score names three lifts in one line and five in the next
what: With no score yet, the Strength score says 'Do a bench press, squat or deadlift in a workout and your score shows here.' The i beside the same heading says the score is built from bench press, squat, deadlift, overhead press and row, and an overhead press or a row alone does give a score. The two lines disagree.
expected: The empty line names the same five lifts as the i, or says 'one of the main lifts'.
how_often: every time the empty score shows
fix_line: Name all five lifts in the empty line

title: The Target line uses other words than the rest of the app for body weight and machine help
what: The Target line says 'First time, bodyweight, 8-12 reps' (one word) while every other screen says 'body weight'. On assisted lifts the Target line shows 'Assist 20 kg' and the log column 'ASSIST', but the sentences under it say '20 kg of help', 'Same help' and 'Try it without help'. Two names for the same thing on one card.
expected: One spelling, 'body weight', and one word for machine help on the line and in the reason (for example 'Help 20 kg').
who: members on body-weight and assisted lifts
fix_line: Use the same words on the Target line as in its reason

title: A shared routine file still carries the old app name inside it
what: A routine shared as a file has the MettleUp name in its file name, but the label written inside the file still says ForgeAI, the old app name. Anyone who opens it in a file viewer, or a gym that looks at it, sees the old name. The app checks that label when it opens a file, so changing it must keep old files working.
expected: New files carry the MettleUp name, and the app still opens files that carry the old one.
fix_line: Write a MettleUp kind in new files and accept both when opening
